The clinical summary presents a classic, progressive, multisystem syndrome rooted in advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD). The patient exhibits the full metabolic signature of CKD Stage 4: elevated creatinine (2.3 mg/dL) and BUN (59 mg/dL), metabolic acidosis (HCO₃⁻ 17 mEq/L), hyperkalemia (K⁺ 5.9 mEq/L), hypocalcemia (Ca²⁺ 7.8 mg/dL), hyperphosphatemia (Phos 5.6 mg/dL), anemia with functional iron deficiency (Hb 8 g/dL, ferritin 42 ng/mL), and mild hypoalbuminemia — all consistent with uremic milieu and disordered mineral bone metabolism. The symptoms — progressive generalized weakness and unintentional weight loss — are fully explained by established uremic pathophysiology: anemia-induced tissue hypoxia, acidosis-driven muscle catabolism, hyperkalemia-related neuromuscular fatigue, and chronic systemic catabolism. No other unifying diagnosis accounts for *all* the laboratory, metabolic, hematologic, and clinical findings with equal parsimony and fidelity.

- Hypocalcemia (Ca²⁺ 7.8 mg/dL) and hyperphosphatemia (Phos 5.6 mg/dL) reflect CKD-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD).  
- Anemia (Hb 8 g/dL, Hct 29%, ferritin 42 ng/mL) is consistent with anemia of chronic kidney disease and functional iron deficiency.

- Parathyroid hormone (PTH) level — pending but highly relevant to confirm secondary hyperparathyroidism and guide CKD-MBD management.  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Chronic Kidney Disease, Stage 4, due to hypertensive nephrosclerosis
